question: What does Spring Boot auto-configuration primarily do?

options.text: Automatically writes application business logic
Configures beans based on classpath contents, existing beans, and configuration properties
Creates a new database for every application
Disables explicit configuration

explanation: Auto-configuration contributes configuration when its conditions match. It commonly checks available classes, properties, and whether an application has already supplied a bean. Developers can override defaults by defining their own configuration.

question: What is a Spring Boot starter?

options.text: A curated dependency descriptor that brings in a useful set of related dependencies
A Java class that starts every bean manually
A replacement for the Spring container
A production deployment server

explanation: Starters simplify dependency management by grouping commonly used libraries for a capability, such as web, validation, data JPA, or security.

question: Which annotation is commonly used to enable a configuration class only when a class is present on the classpath?

options.text: @ConditionalOnClass
@Primary
@Order
@Lazy

explanation: `@ConditionalOnClass` is one of Boot's condition annotations. It allows configuration to match only when specified classes are available, helping auto-configuration adapt to the application's dependencies.

question: What does `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` typically allow an auto-configuration to do?

options.text: Create a default bean only when the application has not already provided a matching bean
Create a bean only when a database row is missing
Disable all user-defined beans
Force two beans to have the same name

explanation: It backs off when a matching bean already exists, allowing application-specific beans to replace Boot defaults.

question: How can a developer inspect which auto-configurations matched or did not match during startup?

options.text: Use the condition evaluation report, for example by enabling the debug startup report
Read the JVM heap dump only
Enable SQL logging only
Inspect the browser developer console

explanation: Boot can print a condition evaluation report when debug mode is enabled. Actuator's conditions endpoint may also expose condition information when appropriately configured and secured.

question: What is the purpose of `@ConditionalOnProperty`?

options.text: To apply configuration when a specified property has a matching value or is present, depending on its settings
To validate every HTTP request body
To map a Java field to a database column
To select a transaction isolation level

explanation: `@ConditionalOnProperty` lets configuration be enabled or disabled through environment properties, often using a feature flag such as `feature.audit.enabled=true`.

question: What is the recommended modern mechanism for registering custom auto-configuration in a Spring Boot library?

options.text: List the auto-configuration class in `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports`
Add it only to `web.xml`
Put it in the root package and rely on component scanning by every consumer
Register it in the JVM manifest

explanation: Modern Spring Boot versions use the `AutoConfiguration.imports` resource to list auto-configuration classes. Older Boot versions used `spring.factories` for this purpose.

question: Why should auto-configuration classes generally avoid broad component scanning?

options.text: Broad scanning can unexpectedly register application components from packages that the library does not own
Component scanning prevents conditional annotations from working
It makes all beans prototype scoped
It disables configuration properties

explanation: Library auto-configuration should be explicit and narrowly scoped. Broad scanning can cause bean collisions and surprising side effects in consuming applications.

question: What is the purpose of `@AutoConfiguration` in recent Spring Boot versions?

options.text: It marks a class as an auto-configuration candidate
It marks a controller as reactive
It enables database migrations
It turns a class into a test fixture

explanation: `@AutoConfiguration` is a specialized configuration annotation intended for Boot auto-configuration classes. It communicates the class's role and supports ordering metadata.

question: What is a practical reason to exclude a specific auto-configuration?

options.text: The application intentionally supplies an alternative or does not want that integration configured
The application needs to increase HTTP request throughput automatically
The application wants to skip Java compilation
The application wants to remove all Spring beans

explanation: Exclusions are useful when a default integration is unwanted or conflicts with an intentional alternative. They should be targeted rather than used as a substitute for understanding configuration conditions.
